columns.title: IP (IPv4/IPv6)
columns.profile: IPv4 or IPv6 datagram service / ICMP; numeric destinations; no application TCP/UDP/TLS/QUIC or IPsec, NAT or stateful firewall; optional transit traffic-history/export disabled. Global unicast control: TCP / BGP-4 + MP-BGP. F12: IGMP/MLD + PIM-SM. Independent deployment: RFC 1918 private IPv4 or locally generated IPv6 ULA, locally provisioned routes. Global Internet allocation remains a separate requirement. F09: optional per-packet unicast next-hop rotation over provisioned multiple routes (RFC 2991), not merely flow-hashed ECMP; G04: multiple BGP reflector clusters and group-scoped PIM RPs.; C06: separate IPv6 client contexts with distinct randomized temporary sources under a shared multi-host prefix, no stable source/DNS identity or host-identifying flow-label policy reused; no continuity or on-link anonymity claim F37 witness: optional router-local AQM with congestion-dependent packet dropping (RFC 7567), without requiring application TCP or ECN feedback. F38 witness: IP-layer DiffServ domains with participant-operated classifiers, policing/shaping and priority service under local provisioning and inter-domain traffic agreements (RFC 2475). These explicitly selected router policies do not imply default Internet deployment or add RSVP/IntServ application reservations, stateful firewalling or a new transport layer.

columns.title: Secure DTN
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / TCPCLv4 / BPv7 + BPSec; independent private IPv4 and RFC 9758 private-use ipn domain; known EIDs, aggregate gateway exits, locally agreed dtn collective names, numeric peers; participant-operated CAs, local trust and BPSec keys, NODE-ID validation, no online OCSP or SNI; optional TLS padding, concurrent proactive forwarding and static collective fanout credited architecturally; independent logical-node EIDs/certificates/BPSec keys per context, no cross-context TLS resumption; discard completed bundles, no retained report archive or transit traffic history G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities. F21: ION native BPSec receive-API witness at 154a4cc7354b26661169f8d8b75a4002cd509a9f; exact source-EID/key bindings, distinct pairwise HMAC keys held only by each original sender and receiver, BIBs over primary and payload, primary-inclusive payload integrity scope; application treats bundleSourceEid as authenticated only when both native verification indicators are true. No application authentication exchange, group key or relay-held origin key; no F16 admission/revocation guarantee inferred. F16 alternative witness: ION 154a4cc with optional BSL 468db9b enabled and mandatory APPOUT wildcard-source BIB verification over primary and payload. One authorized remote sender at a time; a fresh secret key is held only by that sender and the final receiver, never transit. Native policy uses a locally fixed key-registry identifier. Revocation uses completed shutdown of receiver and consumers, a fresh empty bundle/fragment/delivery store and a fresh key provisioned only to the newly authorized sender. No hot revocation, simultaneous independent-key allowlist, or claimed source-EID authentication is inferred from this witness; F21 retains its separate exact-source policy. F37/F38: optional router-local AQM and independent DiffServ domain enforcement selected in the existing IPv4/TCP transport beneath TLS/TCPCLv4. Policies apply to visible transport aggregates, without inspecting bundles or BPSec payloads. This does not resolve BPv7/SABR priority mapping, application reservation, DTN storage congestion or complete executable integration; no corresponding IP layer is added to the separate LTP/AOS column.

Exact-origin pairwise keys, primary and payload integrity coverage, and application checks of both verification flags are required. This pins these BP-layer mechanisms only; complete TCPCL/TLS or LTP/Encapsulation/AOS integration, critical metadata propagation at later hops, custody mapping and simultaneous on-wire path use remain unqualified. This final BP delivery gate is independent of the chosen CGR route and TCPCL ingress. C06 capability witness uses separate logical contexts with independently provisioned private-domain EIDs, certificates, BPSec keys and stores; no cross-context TLS resumption or common certificate subject/serial is required. columns.title: I2P
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / NTCP2 / I2P destinations and tunnels; locally supplied fresh RouterInfo bundle, numeric NTCP2 contacts and known destination keys; multiple active outbound tunnels with at least two remote hops, tunneled destination lookups; correct local clock; no online reseed or external naming service; isolated router/destination key contexts without shared family declarations; independent private IPv4 with i2np.allowLocal and local bootstrap/network configuration; concurrent-tunnel policy is architectural, ordinary Java per-pair selection is sticky; transit-only C08 role with optional identity-bearing traffic/debug history disabled G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities. The Yes covers hybrid-established traffic, not the initial New Session payload or classical-type sessions; no universal fail-closed policy is inferred. columns.title: Basic Nostr
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / HTTP Upgrade / WebSocket / NIP-01; optional TLS padding credited architecturally; WSS relay hostnames resolved through DNS; regular events proactively published concurrently over two independent relay paths; separate author contexts; no NIP-17/44/42 or secret-gated camouflage; F21: verified event author to reader, not live publishing connection or relay identity; G01 global deployment: WSS relays over conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet C08: operator-controlled nostr-rs-relay at b5c1f642e4f4c3b9c54f5d18d66f4c53642076b4, SQLite in_memory=true, bundled URI-enabled SQLite and memory temporary storage; no file logging, persistent WSS-proxy logs, diagnostics export, swap, dumps, hibernation or snapshots. Use a stable relay hostname resolving to its assigned host address, separate WebSocket connections, and a subscription to the publishing process author key. Local IP delivery keeps this relay leg on-host; the same author filter and EVENT/REQ interface deliver to a remote subscriber connection. Separate from C04 CLIENT/ALL probe witness. NodeInfo is an existing request/response service; allow its normal response policy and throttling. Other criterion-specific serial and security configurations remain unchanged.

columns.title: IP / Babel
columns.profile: IPv6 datagram service / ICMPv6; control plane IPv6 / UDP / Babel RFC 8966. columns.title: IPv6 IoT / RPL
columns.profile: 6LoWPAN (RFC 4944/6282) / IPv6 / RPL (RFC 6550, non-storing downward routing with RFC 6554, OF0 RFC 6552) / UDP / DTLS 1.3 (RFC 9147). IEEE 802.15.4 link binding; endpoint leaf role, participant-operated RPL root and routers. Locally provisioned ULA prefix, numeric peer addresses, 6LoWPAN neighbor discovery RFC 6775. RPL unsecured mode on an access-controlled link; DTLS does not protect routing control. End-to-end DTLS with distinct locally provisioned pairwise external PSKs, psk_ke and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256; no 0-RTT, tickets or application authentication overlay. Fresh PSK handshakes allowed; no forward-secrecy claim for this PSK-only choice. No DNS, public CA, cloud broker, CoAP or MQTT dependency. No DTLS-terminating gateway: the final peers hold the traffic keys. Documentary composition; complete executable integration and sleep/overhead behavior remain unqualified. C03 configuration: enable IEEE 802.15.4 AES-128-CCM link security at level 7 (ENC-MIC128) for all established data frames carrying 6LoWPAN, including RPL unicast and multicast control, on every observed adjacency. Provision link keys locally, including a key usable for multicast delivery, and maintain non-repeating frame counters. This credits a passive radio observer without link keys; MAC headers remain visible and authorized routers decrypt RPL controls. RPL remains in unsecured mode; final-pair DTLS keys stay separate. F37/F38 architectural witnesses: optional router-local IPv6 AQM with congestion-dependent dropping (RFC 7567), and independently administered IPv6 DiffServ conditioning and per-hop service (RFC 2474/2475). RFC 6282 Traffic Class compression preserves non-elided DSCP information. Apply policy at participant-operated forwarding nodes; no DTLS termination, new transport or default embedded implementation is implied. Full executable integration remains unqualified as elsewhere in this profile.

columns.title: HIPv2 / ESP
columns.profile: IPv4 or IPv6 / HIPv2 control (RFC 7401) and ESP-protected user traffic (RFC 7402), with host mobility RFC 8046. Independent deployment uses private IPv4, known numeric initial locators and pinned peer Host Identities/HITs; locally generated ECDSA P-256 identities, ECDH P-256, HIP ECDSA/SHA-384 HIT suite 2 and ESP AES-128-CBC with HMAC-SHA-256 (transform 8). Ordinary application UDP is carried inside the protected host-to-host data path, not as a HIP underlay tunnel. No DNS, rendezvous service, external CA, NAT-traversal extension or application authentication wrapper is selected. One moving endpoint with a reachable known peer; no simultaneous-mobility guarantee. Documentary composition; exact executable integration remains unqualified. G01 global deployment: conventional IPv6 Internet underlay with BGP/MP-BGP prefix routing, matching IP, PRP-over-IP and Multipath QUIC. Independent private deployment remains the separate S03/S04 capability; adjacent-only private IP meshes are not this global case. Global plausibility uses IPv6; retained private deployments and historical runtime/budget witnesses use IPv4. F37/F38: optional router-local AQM and independently administered DiffServ domains explicitly selected in the IP forwarding layer carrying HIP/ESP. Classification may use visible IP transport aggregates without decrypting ESP; no extra tunnel or application QoS reservation. F39 application-binding witness: use HIT-valued socket endpoints under the RFC 5338 application model, with the service bound to its chosen local HIT and UDP port. RFC 5338 explicitly describes connections to a local HIT. Apply that identifier/socket model to the selected HIPv2 identities; no legacy HIP wire version, old HIT hash suite, new resolver dependency or different remote ESP suite is imported.

columns.title: CCNx 1.0
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / CCNx 1.0 semantics RFC 8569 and TLV encoding RFC 8609. Independent deployment uses private IPv4, numeric adjacent forwarders, locally configured name-prefix FIB entries and known content names. Producer Content Objects use ECDSA-SHA256 signatures with locally generated keys explicitly trusted by consumers; no externally mandated name registry or certificate authority selected. Interests use CRC32C integrity checks, not authenticated consumer identities. In-network matching, pending Interests and caching follow CCNx semantics. No TLS, encrypted-session extension, application authentication wrapper or NDN/NLSR extension is added. Dynamic routing and automatic global name discovery are not silently supplied by static FIB configuration. Documentary composition; executable integration remains unqualified. G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching IP, PRP-over-IP and Multipath QUIC. Independent private deployment remains the separate S03/S04 capability; adjacent-only private IP meshes are not this global case. F37/F38: optional native RFC 8569 Interest Return behavior explicitly selected: locally congested forwarders discard Interests and report Congestion; preceding forwarders handle returns under section 10.3, including alternative next-hop selection when available. Per-forwarder name/interface ACLs and Prohibited handling selected under 10.3.6. Documentary capability, not measured congestion performance or executable integration. F39 bounded request/reply witness: one producer process owns the chosen globally scoped name prefix; use previously unrequested names with no matching cached response and configure the prefix toward that producer. The same name-based exchange reaches a local producer attachment or a remote producer through the selected network. No RPC framework, process migration, exactly-once execution, arbitrary duplex stream or new authentication layer is added.

columns.title: LISP
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / LISP (RFC 9300 data plane and RFC 9301 control plane) / inner IPv4 / application UDP; configured EID prefixes and RLOCs; numeric peer and mapping-service addresses; participant-operated Map-Resolver and Map-Server with locally provisioned registration keys. No LISP-SEC, endpoint TLS/IPsec, or application identity layer selected. F09 architectural witness: two reachable best-priority RLOCs with zero weights, both delivering to the same destination EID; the ITR alternates successive useful packets of one UDP communication between them. Keep the outer UDP source port stable for the inner flow. Distinct provisioned underlay routes are required; no modified wire format or claimed implementation default. F37/F38: optional router-local AQM and independently administered DiffServ domains explicitly selected in the outer IPv4 transport. Outer packet conditioning/classification; RFC 9300 DSCP handling retained. No RSVP/IntServ or application reservation added.

columns.title: ILNPv6
columns.profile: ILNPv6 / TCP with ILNP identifier-only transport binding (RFC 6740 and RFC 6741); IPv6-compatible packet format with distinct 64-bit Identifier and Locator semantics, not an outer IPv6 tunnel; RFC 6743 Locator Updates and RFC 6744 Nonce Destination Option; locally generated NIDs, Router Advertisements and neighbour discovery; DNS NID/L64 discovery per RFC 6742. Host mobility between authorized attachments with overlap, a stationary reachable correspondent, and unchanged NIDs during the TCP connection. No IPsec, TLS, CGA identity binding or multipath TCP selected. Experimental specification; executable composition not qualified. F37/F38: optional local AQM and independently administered DiffServ policies explicitly selected in the IPv6-compatible forwarding plane; Traffic Class retained, no extra outer IP tunnel. No RSVP/IntServ or application reservation added. F39 application witness: a well-behaved socket application retains a participant name and TCP service port; ILNP-aware resolution supplies the current Identifier-Locator vector. A local service listens on its assigned vector or wildcard. Host-local routing delivers to the co-resident service; remote delivery uses the same naming/socket model and identifier-bound transport. No application switch to localhost or AF_UNIX is required. The pinned public Linux ILNP prototype corroborates local-path plausibility; its static-hosts resolver setup is not claimed as a runtime validation of the selected DNS NID/L64 composition.

columns.title: Tailscale
columns.profile: Tailscale Linux clients using WireGuard over UDP/IP on the routed Internet; Tailscale-managed coordination and an external identity provider for user enrollment. Tailnet Lock enabled with participant-controlled signing nodes; explicit restrictive network grants. Direct node-to-node payload paths with DERP/TLS relay fallback, ending at the two Tailscale nodes. Standard TUN client, not tsnet or userspace proxy mode. No Headscale, subnet/exit-node endpoint substitution, application TLS, content protocol or additional preshared post-quantum secret selected. Documentary profile, not a pinned runtime certification. F37/F38: explicitly selected optional router-local AQM and independently administered DiffServ domains on outer IP transport, classifying tunnel/DERP connection aggregates without inspecting encrypted inner traffic. No application QoS reservation or requirement to copy inner DSCP; not universal public-network deployment.

columns.title: RINA
columns.profile: RINA application flows over recursively composed normal DIFs, with an Ethernet shim at the bottom; participant-operated enrollment and management, locally configured application names and DIF membership. Select QoS-aware flow allocation and per-DIF congestion-control policies acting on aggregate lower-layer flows. IRATI/Linux is the implementation reference for subsequent qualification, not a claim that a pinned executable configuration has been validated. No IP shim, external naming authority or application security wrapper is supplied; selected native modes are stated explicitly below. Current positive entries establish documented architectural mechanisms; implementation coverage, security and operational adoption require separate evidence. Mobility witness: additionally select the native Wi-Fi shim and local mobman two-provider make-before-break policy documented in IRATI Tutorial 10, with two interfaces and preconfigured DIF membership. This is a bounded mobility mode, not an IP overlay or a validated combined deployment; no security suite is imported from the demonstrator. Redundant-path mode: additionally select native static routing with two entries for the same destination/QoS and distinct next hops, default PDUFT generation and default PFF/RMT, over provisioned loop-free paths converging on one receiving IPCP. Source inspection establishes proactive copying; this is an explicit optional mode, not the default Dijkstra or the per-flow multipath plugin. Use a DTCP-enabled flow when duplicate handling is required; complete duplicate/reordering behavior and the combined deployment remain untested. Authentication mode: select native PSOC_authentication-ssh2 version 1 for IPCP enrollment, locally generated RSA keys of at least 2048 bits and locally provisioned peer-name/public-key bindings, with EDH, AES256, SHA256 and deflate under default SDU protection. The pinned code implements finite-field ephemeral DH, despite the README elliptic-curve wording. This custom SSH2-inspired mechanism is not asserted to be SSH interoperability or an audited modern security construction. Authentication scope is the enrolled IPCP; final application identity exposure remains a separate qualification; end-host content protection requires the upper-DIF placement specified below. No post-quantum KEM is selected. End-host confidentiality mode: place an additional normal DIF with only the two endpoint-host IPCPs above the routed transit DIFs; select the declared SSH2-inspired authentication and AES256 SDU protection between these two members. Applications register to this upper DIF. Transit nodes participate only in lower DIFs and do not hold the upper-DIF keys. This native recursive composition is an architectural/source-supported option, not a validated combined deployment. The endpoint OS/IPCP is trusted; protection between mutually untrusted applications sharing that OS is not claimed. For passive established-traffic assessment, enable the selected SDU encryption on every normal-DIF adjacency, including the lowest normal DIF above Ethernet/Wi-Fi; no plaintext normal-DIF adjacency exception is selected. Link framing and bootstrap remain outside the encrypted normal-DIF PDU.

criteria.title: Operates without IPv4/IPv6 throughout the stack
criteria.definition: No mandatory IP layer, including operational support.
criteria.research_action: Fix non-IP binding, bootstrap and support dependencies; run without IP.

criteria.title: Needs no participant IP address configuration
criteria.definition: Participant-facing addressing uses a self-generated address or a non-IP participant namespace; no assigned participant IP address is needed at that layer. Underlay and relay transport IP configuration are excluded uniformly and remain assessed by F01/F03. This is not zero-configuration deployment: other identifiers, peers, trust and permissions may need provisioning.
criteria.research_action: Trace endpoint creation and bootstrap; distinguish application and underlay configuration.

criteria.title: Routed operation needs no topology-dependent address configuration
criteria.definition: No network-prefix, subnet or locator assignment tied to attachment in the selected stack, including its underlay. DHCP/SLAAC automate such configuration rather than remove it. Locally generated identities and session-local forwarding labels do not count. Excludes route policy, trust, permissions and physical/link setup.
criteria.research_action: Trace address assignment across the selected stack; distinguish topology-dependent locators from self-generated identities and local forwarding labels. F02 concerns participant provisioning; F03 concerns the routed network as a whole.

criteria.title: Cryptographic reference independent of location
criteria.definition: Participant or service reference verifiable independently of its locator; not necessarily self-certifying.
criteria.research_action: Trace reference creation and key binding; distinguish identity, certificate and locator.

criteria.title: Peer continuity and authorization across sessions
criteria.definition: A peer continuity and authorization context survives the end of a session and a change of carrier. No particular object name, data structure or protocol-specific lifecycle is required. A stable identity key alone does not establish retained authorization context.
criteria.research_action: Establish what peer continuity and authorization state survives session termination and carrier changes, and how it is reused for a later session. Evaluate documented behavior regardless of implementation terminology; a stable key alone is insufficient.

criteria.title: Encrypts content between communicating endpoints
criteria.definition: Protection between the compared endpoints, not merely a transit link.
criteria.research_action: Fix the end-to-end profile and key custody; identify every encryption termination point.

criteria.title: Cryptographically authenticates a remote participant
criteria.definition: Remote identity or signed authorship proof; does not imply civil identity, mutual authentication or current presence.
criteria.research_action: Specify whose identity is proved, to whom, and whether proof covers a live session or stored message.

criteria.title: Preserves a transport connection across path changes
criteria.definition: The same connection survives; reconnecting with the same contact does not qualify. UDP alone has no connection.
criteria.research_action: Define address/path change and connection lifetime; test continuity, replay and reordering.

criteria.title: Uses simultaneous paths for one communication
criteria.definition: Concurrent useful data paths, rather than sequential failover or probes.
criteria.research_action: Fix scheduler, path policy and extension; distinguish multiple sessions from one communication.

criteria.title: Proactively duplicates data across distinct paths
criteria.definition: Intentional redundancy before loss, rather than retransmission after loss.
criteria.research_action: Find replication and deduplication rules; test physically diverse paths and resource costs.

criteria.title: Retains messages for delivery after disconnection
criteria.definition: Deferred delivery storage, not transient transport buffers.
criteria.research_action: Check persistence, expiry, capacity and recovery without a contemporaneous path.

criteria.title: Multicast replication at network forwarders
criteria.definition: One-to-many network forwarding; application-relay fanout does not qualify. BP selects static collective fanout with implementation qualification pending.
criteria.research_action: Fix multicast routing and replication; distinguish broadcast, flooding and application pubsub.

criteria.title: Group with multiple authorized senders and continuity across sessions
criteria.definition: Multiple authorized participants can send to a group. Membership and group authority are distributed, and group continuity is independent of individual session lifetimes. Matching terminology or a particular implementation is not required.
criteria.research_action: Identify sender authorization, membership and distributed authority rules; trace group continuity across session termination and subsequent participation. Apply the same behavioral requirements to every selected stack.

criteria.title: Explicit goal of concealing endpoint location
criteria.definition: Location-hiding mechanism; not immunity to global correlation.
criteria.research_action: Define observer and profile; inventory visible identity, adjacency and location metadata.

criteria.title: Architectural protection of processing and state against unauthorized traffic
criteria.definition: The selected composition provides a documented admission or early-rejection mechanism together with bounded state or computational work at an identified protected boundary. Identify pre-admission CPU, memory, queue and state costs, the work deferred until admission, and the required local policy. Native configurable mechanisms may qualify within selected layers. Encryption, finite hardware or an anti-amplification byte cap alone does not qualify. Yes credits scoped architectural protection, not a measured service floor or protection from every admitted attacker. Link-capacity protection is assessed separately in F26.
criteria.method: Primary specification and source analysis; experiments are complementary
criteria.research_action: Identify CPU/state admission ordering and bounds; evaluate downstream link authorization separately in F26.

criteria.title: Controls final-peer access without external firewall
criteria.definition: Final-peer network payload admission: allow locally authorized cryptographic peers, deny others before application payload delivery, and revoke old authority at a completed local cutover, including active paths and pending delivery. Native policy hooks and administrative teardown/restart are allowed; authorized service must remain available after cutover. Already delivered data, application-operation permissions, handshake/probe traffic, unrelated host services and DoS isolation are outside scope. Added application authentication or payload filtering is not credited.
criteria.research_action: Trace native final-peer admission and revocation at completed local cutover; see round063.html#policy.

criteria.title: Operates without DNS
criteria.definition: No DNS from bootstrap through authorized traffic; names absent from packets alone are insufficient.
criteria.research_action: Fix peers, discovery, certificates and dependencies; initialize without DNS queries.

criteria.title: DTN forwarding across discontinuous contacts
criteria.definition: Network intermediaries retain and later forward an admitted item across non-overlapping contacts, without a contemporaneous complete end-to-end path. A mailbox at a common server, transport buffering or reconnection alone does not qualify. Previously established trust and bounded expiry are allowed.
criteria.research_action: Trace A-to-B followed by B-to-C with no overlapping contacts, intermediate storage, expiry, cryptographic viability and duplicate handling; distinguish architecture from executable activation.

criteria.title: Transit forwarding without per-end-to-end-flow state
criteria.definition: Transit can forward without a mandatory entry for each end-to-end flow or circuit. Routes, neighbor sessions and aggregate multicast state are allowed. Endpoint transport state is outside this transit-only test. Include selected overlay relays, not only the IP underlay.
criteria.research_action: Inventory every selected transit role and its state keys/lifetimes. Distinguish aggregate routes and neighbor sessions from endpoint-flow/circuit entries and optional caches.

criteria.title: Identify the communicating peer without extra application authentication
criteria.definition: The selected stack authenticates the final communicating peer and exposes that identity to the receiving application bound to the communication, without an added application authentication exchange. Neighbor identity, unauthenticated addresses or an unbound claim are insufficient. This does not supply civil identity, account roles, permissions or transit anonymity.
criteria.research_action: Trace proof validation, application-visible identity and binding to the received channel/item. Separate final peer from relays, object authors and security sources; inspect close/rekey and stale-reference behavior.

criteria.title: Shared-reference discovery of independent participants
criteria.definition: One shared reference can discover multiple independently identified participants, without an exclusive controller of that reference or a shared private identity. A bounded candidate set is sufficient; exhaustive enumeration and simultaneous delivery are not required. Only mechanisms in the declared stack count. Self-declaration does not establish membership legitimacy, service authorization or current availability.
criteria.research_action: Trace reference formation, independent declarations, multi-candidate lookup and candidate identity binding. Separate routing fanout, anycast and content retrieval from participant discovery; do not silently add a discovery application or module.

criteria.title: Endpoint mobility without infrastructure routing control
criteria.definition: Supports an endpoint changing attachment or access network while preserving its peer identity and ongoing logical communication, without requiring the application to establish a new peer relationship or reconstruct communication. The endpoint must not need administrative control of infrastructure routes, prefix origination or an AS; moving an administratively controlled network with the endpoint does not qualify. Normal participant attachment, path authentication and automatic protocol signaling are allowed, including signaling intrinsic to a mesh or overlay; merely running routing code does not disqualify a participant. Ordinary network access permission is not authority to originate infrastructure routes. Evaluate a supported endpoint role and state its limits; client-only support can qualify. Mere route repair with stationary endpoints, or retaining an identifier while restarting communication, is insufficient. Lossless handover, simultaneous mobility of both endpoints and indefinite disconnection are not required. Only mechanisms in the declared stack count.
criteria.research_action: Move an ordinary participant between attachments with no new infrastructure route/prefix/AS privileges. Trace retained identity and communication state, automatic locator/path updates and application-visible behavior. List access permissions separately from routing authority. Exclude administrator-driven prefix/AS relocation. Record role, interruption, loss and timeout; test existing runtime qualifications separately.

criteria.title: Reception coordinated with endpoint sleep periods
criteria.definition: An endpoint may suspend transmission and reception during planned periods and wake at known opportunities to receive data. The sender or an intermediary responsible for delivery coordinates attempts with those opportunities, retaining data when necessary. The mechanism lets the receiver determine when to listen without remaining continuously active. Reconnecting on wake, receiver-initiated periodic polling, or retransmissions unaware of receiver availability do not suffice. Custody alone does not suffice without coordinated delivery. F27 separately evaluates negotiation of communication windows.
criteria.method: Reassessment required under owner-approved definition; historical verdict not carried forward
criteria.research_action: Identify how the receiver learns wake/listen opportunities, who coordinates delivery, which traffic follows the schedule, and retention/expiry behavior. Specify clock or relative timing, tolerance and schedule changes. Do not inherit old F24 reenrollment evidence or F25 byte budgets; no measured energy saving is implied.

criteria.title: Prevents unauthorized traffic from consuming downstream link capacity
criteria.definition: The selected composition provides a native transit admission or authorization check before transmission on an identified onward link. Traffic lacking the required local forwarding authority is rejected or constrained there, protecting subsequent links from that traffic. Identify the enforcement point, onward links protected, required policy and costs already incurred upstream. Local adjacency or forwarding authority may suffice; intermediaries need not know final endpoint identity. Endpoint-only filtering, encryption, receiver flow control and congestion control alone do not qualify. Yes does not imply protection of the ingress medium already traversed, RF-jamming resistance, guaranteed bandwidth or containment of every authorized attacker. Missing boundary evidence remains Pending; No applies only to the selected composition.
criteria.method: Primary architectural and forwarding-policy analysis; no bandwidth benchmark required
criteria.research_action: Locate the transit authorization check before onward transmission; identify protected downstream links and the remaining ingress exposure.

criteria.title: Negotiated communication windows
criteria.definition: The selected composition explicitly provides for participants to agree on temporal availability windows for transmission and periods of inactivity between them. The transmitter follows the agreed receiver availability rather than relying only on retries after disappearance. Identify the negotiating roles, protocol layer and carrier dependency. A scoped architectural requirement can qualify; unspecified procedures, timing parameters or wire formats must remain explicit qualifications. Local sleep timers, congestion windows, generic buffering and reconnection alone do not qualify. This does not by itself establish uninterrupted cryptographic-session retention or measured energy savings.
criteria.method: Primary architectural or protocol evidence; distinguish specified capability from executable realization
criteria.research_action: Identify the availability-window agreement, acceptance and direction; document duration/spacing, clock basis, changes, expiry, pending-data handling and which data/control/cover traffic obeys it. Distinguish retained relationships, logical connections and cryptographic sessions. No result is inherited from F18, F24 or F25.

criteria.title: Explicit endpoint path selection
criteria.definition: The sending endpoint can select a forwarding path or constrain the intermediaries used for its communication, beyond choosing only the destination or local access interface. Identify the exposed granularity, such as nodes, domains or path segments, and how the selected path is enforced. Selection among paths offered by infrastructure may qualify; independent path discovery is not required. Automatic multipath scheduling without endpoint path control does not qualify. This does not establish knowledge of hidden underlay hops or freedom from all routing authorities.
criteria.method: Primary architectural or protocol evidence for the selected composition; distinguish capability from execution
criteria.research_action: Identify the endpoint interface for selecting or excluding intermediaries, available path information, enforcement and failure behavior. State path granularity and remaining infrastructure dependencies. Distinguish F09 concurrent paths and F23 mobility.

criteria.title: Named-content retrieval without prior server selection
criteria.definition: A requester can use a content reference to discover or reach a suitable supplier, replica or cache without selecting the serving endpoint beforehand. Direct named-data forwarding and reference-based supplier discovery can both qualify. The selected profile must bind the reference to the requested content; generic participant discovery alone is insufficient. Subsequent application transfer is allowed and must be disclosed. Host-name resolution alone does not qualify. Content authenticity and cross-requester caching are assessed separately.
criteria.method: Primary architectural or protocol evidence for the selected composition; distinguish capability from execution
criteria.research_action: Identify the content-reference binding, supplier discovery or forwarding mechanism, and who chooses the serving source. Disclose any profile convention and application transfer. Do not require one information-centric wire design; distinguish F22 generic participant discovery, F30 verification and F31 caching.

criteria.title: Verify content authenticity independently of its delivery connection
criteria.definition: The selected composition supplies object-level cryptographic evidence that lets a recipient verify an object against an authorized origin or trusted reference after delivery through an intermediary or a different connection. Evidence must remain bound to the object rather than solely to the live transport. A signature, suitable MAC or digest bound to an independently trusted reference may qualify within its stated trust model. A bare checksum or a hash received only from the untrusted supplier does not establish authenticity. Public verification by arbitrary recipients is not required.
criteria.method: Primary architectural or protocol evidence for the selected composition; distinguish capability from execution
criteria.research_action: Identify the protected object and metadata, verification evidence, trust/reference acquisition and verifier roles. Check verification after forwarding or storage. Distinguish origin authentication, reference integrity and freshness; do not infer replay protection or civil identity.

criteria.title: Serve other requesters from an intermediate copy
criteria.definition: An intermediary in the selected composition can retain a reusable content object and satisfy a later request by another requester from that copy, avoiding a new transfer from the original source. Describe cache admission, lookup, serving and validity rules. Storage dedicated to forwarding one queued message to its original recipient, retransmission buffers and caching supplied only by an unselected application do not qualify. Persistence across restarts and guaranteed cache hits are not required.
criteria.method: Primary architectural or protocol evidence for the selected composition; distinguish capability from execution
criteria.research_action: Identify a cross-requester cache-serving path, object matching, authorization and freshness or expiry rules. Distinguish F11 deferred messages, F18 discontinuous contacts and F29 named retrieval. Document source-transfer savings without inventing a hit rate.

criteria.title: Route planning using future contacts and capacity
criteria.definition: The selected composition can compute or select a route using known or predicted future contact opportunities and their usable transfer capacities, so that forwarding decisions account for when a link will exist and whether it can carry the item. Externally supplied plans may qualify; participants need not negotiate the contacts. Merely waiting for connectivity, using current link costs, or accepting a local transmission timetable without route planning does not qualify.
criteria.method: Primary architectural or protocol evidence for the selected composition; distinguish capability from execution
criteria.research_action: Identify contact times, rates or volumes, route computation and capacity feasibility. Document plan provenance, clock assumptions, stale-plan handling and capacity accounting. Distinguish F18 store-and-forward and F27 negotiated windows; do not infer guaranteed delivery.

criteria.title: Reliable transfer adapted to prolonged delay and interruption
criteria.definition: The selected composition provides retransmission-based reliable transfer with documented timer or recovery behavior adapted to prolonged propagation delays and interruptions of the transfer opportunity. Explicit suspension/resumption of recovery timers or another specified mechanism can qualify. Ordinary short-outage retries, arbitrary enlargement of a timeout, or storage without reliable-transfer recovery are insufficient. Identify the supported delay/interruption conditions and state retained; no unlimited outage tolerance is implied.
criteria.method: Primary architectural or protocol evidence for the selected composition; distinguish capability from execution
criteria.research_action: Identify acknowledgment/checkpoint and retransmission behavior, delay estimation, contact-loss signals, timer suspension or equivalent adaptation, resumption and expiry limits. Distinguish F18 routing/storage, F24 endpoint reenrollment and F27 negotiated availability. Assess protocol capability separately from performance measurements.

criteria.title: Connect existing endpoints through a transparent bridge
criteria.definition: Integration with existing networks: the selected composition bridges layer-2 frames across multiple forwarding hops while preserving the link service presented to attached endpoints without requiring changes to those endpoints. Identify the supported frame/link type; the existing evaluated service is Ethernet, including unicast, broadcast/multicast, forwarding or learning and MTU constraints. Using Ethernet as a carrier or routing IPv6 ULA packets does not itself provide this service. A hypothetical bridge adapter or unselected tunnel is insufficient. No unlimited broadcast-domain scale is required.
criteria.method: Primary architectural or protocol evidence for the selected composition; distinguish capability from execution
criteria.research_action: Identify endpoint attachment and the multi-hop Ethernet data path, upper-layer transparency, forwarding/loop controls and frame-size limitations. Distinguish F01 non-IP operation and F35 incremental deployment.

criteria.title: Application-requested communication quality
criteria.definition: An application can request communication properties such as capacity, delay or reliability, and the network uses those requirements in flow admission and resource allocation. Identify how requests map to offered service and how unsupported requests are handled. Packet priority marking alone does not qualify. No unconditional performance guarantee is implied.
criteria.method: Primary evidence for the selected composition; identify mechanism, scope and implementation limits
criteria.research_action: Identify the application request interface, admission/allocation decision and service mapping. Distinguish capability from measured guarantees and F32 future-contact route planning.

criteria.title: Congestion control targeted at the affected path segment
criteria.definition: The selected composition can identify a congested intermediate link or bounded network region and adjust traffic at or toward that affected segment. Control may be local or coordinated by the endpoint responsible for the trajectory. Identify the congestion indication, its scope, the controlling participant and the traffic adjustment. A protocol-level capability to report localized saturation and renegotiate traffic at that segment may qualify architecturally. Generic end-to-end loss or delay without localization, static priority alone, and telemetry without an associated control capability do not suffice. No specific wire command, aggregate-flow controller, RINA layer, measured response time or lossless guarantee is required.
criteria.method: Primary evidence for the selected composition; identify mechanism, scope and implementation limits
criteria.research_action: Identify the localized congestion signal or local observation, affected link/region, controller and available traffic adjustment. Endpoint-directed control and intermediate autonomous control are both admissible. Separate capacity negotiation from a response to saturation; distinguish architectural evidence from execution.

criteria.title: Communicate with local or remote participants through the same interface
criteria.definition: Applications communicate with processes on the same host or another host through the same communication abstraction and logical participant references. The stack selects local delivery or a network path without requiring the application to switch IPC APIs or encode the peer physical location. Local zero-copy is an optional optimization, not a requirement. This criterion concerns communication, not process migration or distributed execution.
criteria.method: Architectural mechanism and primary-source review; author declarations explicitly attributed
criteria.research_action: Identify the application interface, logical peer reference, local-delivery mechanism and remote path selection. A shared socket API alone is insufficient if the application must explicitly select localhost versus a remote host address.

criteria.title: Same destination address reachable through an alternative path
criteria.definition: When a path becomes unavailable, the architecture permits reaching the same destination address over another available and authorized path, including through a different destination attachment. The sender need not substitute the address, obtain an alternative address from an external service, or rely on application redirection. Route discovery and fresh session establishment are allowed. A merely physical alternative counts only if the selected protocol can use it. Recovery of transit to an unchanged advertised prefix alone does not establish independence from the destination attachment.
criteria.method: Reassessment required under owner-approved definition; historical verdict not carried forward
criteria.research_action: Identify the stable destination address, failed attachment/path, usable alternative attachment, discovery and forwarding mechanisms. Distinguish transit failure from loss of the attachment associated with an address. State required routing authority/configuration and failure boundaries; no uninterrupted-session requirement.

criteria.title: Conceals the final destination from the first intermediary
criteria.definition: A non-colluding intermediary sees its decrypted state and traffic. Excludes direct endpoint communication.
criteria.research_action: Inventory keys, fields, control queries and forwarding tables; check final identity and location exposure.

criteria.title: Conceals protocol control fields in established traffic
criteria.definition: Passive observation of established protected traffic, excluding bootstrap. Assess exposed control fields and protocol markers; timing/volume inference is separate. This is not a claim of complete protocol indistinguishability.
criteria.research_action: Map cleartext and encrypted established-packet fields, including outer framing; do not use initial bootstrap exposure as a negative.

criteria.title: Includes a defense against active-probe identification
criteria.definition: An uncredentialed adversary probes an endpoint and observes replies and timing; no endpoint compromise.
criteria.research_action: Define valid, invalid and replay probes; inspect disclosures before authorization against a control service.

criteria.title: Bootstraps while external DNS is unavailable
criteria.definition: Initial state as specified in the column, with no DNS cache. Does not cover blocking all peers or directories.
criteria.research_action: Disable DNS before process startup; inventory discovery and trust. F17 is the corresponding functional capability.

criteria.title: Conceals the final-peer association in forwarding identifiers
criteria.definition: A transit observer cannot identify the pair of final interlocutors solely from addresses and flow identifiers visible in established packets. Identifiers on an adjacency may reveal the participants of that segment, but must not directly reveal the final pair or provide a common end-to-end identifier linking that association across observed segments. Evaluate equivalents of the IP five-tuple, circuit labels and connection IDs. Payload encryption with the final pair exposed, or changing identities only between sessions, is insufficient. Timing/volume correlation is assessed separately in C07.
criteria.method: Reassessment required under owner-approved definition; historical verdict not carried forward
criteria.research_action: Inventory visible fields at each selected observation point, including tunnel terminators and participating relays. State observer keys/access and where protection ends; do not infer whole-path protection from one encrypted segment. Trace identifier translation across adjacencies and distinguish local segment identities from final-peer association.

criteria.title: Includes a defense against entry/exit correlation
criteria.definition: Includes a mechanism that reduces observable timing/volume information for cooperating observers. Optional padding or cover traffic can qualify; effectiveness and deployment defaults are separate, and complete correlation prevention is not required.
criteria.research_action: Identify padding, batching, mix or cover mechanisms and their scope; separately measure correlation reduction and cost under a fixed observer model.

criteria.title: Communication without a mandatory separate authority
criteria.definition: Willing peers can communicate from local information without a separate mandatory naming, routing, identity, governance or ledger authority. Network directory authorities and domain certification roles count; counterpart admission policies do not. Underlay allocation is assessed separately.
criteria.research_action: Identify any indispensable third-party approval, registry, consensus signer or trust anchor in the selected network. Test direct operation without that external service.

criteria.title: Participant identity requires no external issuer
criteria.definition: Participants generate a usable cryptographic identity locally; counterparties decide whether to trust or authorize it. Does not imply civil identity.
criteria.research_action: Trace key creation, reference registration and acceptance; determine whether an issuer must authorize creation.

criteria.title: Selected stack needs no external address/name allocation
criteria.definition: Independent deployment needs no public address allocation, DNS delegation or externally assigned domain identifier. Private/local addressing may qualify; Internet reachability is a separate requirement.
criteria.research_action: Fix deployment boundary, private/public underlay and name resolution; inventory allocator and delegation dependencies.

criteria.title: Independent operation under participant-controlled administration
criteria.definition: Participants can deploy and maintain an operational domain with all mandatory control, trust and coordination components under their own administration, without authorization or an indispensable operational service from a specific external vendor or operator. Locally operated authorities are allowed, as is direct peer operation without such authorities. Choosing among external service providers alone does not qualify. This does not guarantee global reachability, freedom from external address allocation, seamless migration or immunity from a local administrator.
criteria.research_action: Inventory bootstrap, enrollment, trust renewal, naming, routing, discovery and coordination dependencies in the selected composition. Establish whether participants can operate all mandatory services and trust roles themselves. Distinguish optional outsourced services from fixed vendor activation, mandatory public directories or external approval. Keep address/name allocation in S03, issuer-free identities in S02 and absence of any separate mandatory authority in S01. Preserve the selected deployment: do not substitute a private clone of a declared public network.

criteria.title: Global reachability without complete global reachability tables
criteria.definition: The complete selected stack permits global reachability without requiring a complete global reachability table at transit nodes or control services. Include prefix, identity and other identifier reachability, and required underlay routing. Moving that table upstream or into a directory does not qualify. Partitioned state is allowed; this is not zero state or a quantitative capacity guarantee.
criteria.research_action: Inventory every transit and control role, including discovery, upper aggregators and the underlay. Establish how arbitrary reachable destinations are located without a mandatory complete global table. A local default route, local labels or a small private deployment alone are insufficient.

criteria.title: Scope-limited updates after participant attachment changes
criteria.definition: A participant attachment change can be accommodated without disseminating its individual identity or location throughout the network. Updates remain within the affected region and participants maintaining relevant communication state, while reachability from elsewhere is preserved. Evaluate a destination that changes attachment, not only an initiating client reconnecting. An example where nothing relevant changes for external routing is insufficient. This evaluates update scope, separately from C01 address reachability and F23 logical communication continuity.
criteria.method: Reassessment required under owner-approved definition; historical verdict not carried forward
criteria.research_action: Trace destination attachment change, affected state, update recipients and reachability from outside the affected region. Include required underlay and control services. Explain what prevents global per-participant dissemination and disclose wider-update cases; do not infer a quantitative convergence or global-capacity guarantee.

criteria.title: Discovery and forwarding without a complete identity catalog at every node
criteria.definition: A transit node can support discovery and forwarding without being required to maintain a complete catalog of final identities in the network. Neighbor records, local relationships, partial caches, aggregates and distributed queries are allowed. A mandatory global hosts.txt-equivalent at each node does not qualify. This consolidates the owner-clarified identity-catalog concern previously discussed as C08; the former C08 traffic-history-retention criterion is retired. G01 separately examines required complete global reachability state anywhere in the selected stack, including control services and underlay.
criteria.method: Reassessment required under owner-approved definition; historical verdict not carried forward
criteria.research_action: Inventory identity state needed for cold discovery and forwarding at each node role; distinguish local/partial records from obligatory complete catalogs. Trace cache misses and distributed lookup. Neither absence of traffic logging nor a low query cost follows automatically; G01/G05 retain their separate scope.

criteria.title: Scale-out without a fixed-capacity coordination point
criteria.definition: Added infrastructure can distribute routing/discovery work without an obligatory single fixed-capacity coordinator. Decentralization alone is insufficient.
criteria.research_action: Map complete-stack coordination dependencies, partitioning, replication and failure recovery.

criteria.title: Plausibility of global operation
criteria.definition: A credible architectural route to a connected network of at least 10 billion devices using contemporary equipment and realistic regional interconnection. Assess namespace, routing/discovery state placement, aggregation, control traffic, search work and update behavior in the selected complete stack. Distributed state and growing aggregate resources are allowed. Documentary mechanisms, resource models, proportional simulations and operational experience can support Yes; world-scale deployment or a full-scale simulation is not required. No requires an evidenced architectural or resource obstruction in the selected composition under the common setting; insufficient evidence remains Pending. Prior targets (1 s discovery, 1 h admission, 99.9% coverage, 5% of domestic 1 Gbit/s per direction, 64 GB per transit equipment and 1000 destinations/device/day) remain sizing references, not jointly certified pass/fail thresholds. Keep identities owned separate from destinations accessed. Use the same Internet-shaped regional infrastructure, population, access workload and contemporary equipment envelope for every composition. Protocol-specific routing, discovery, caching and placement policies may differ on that infrastructure. Do not substitute a more favorable physical topology, omit regions, silently add links or assume an independently chosen cache-hit rate. Count additional equipment and its placement explicitly under the same resource envelope. An evidenced inability to serve this common setting can justify No; impossibility in every imaginable topology is not required. Missing evidence remains Pending.
criteria.method: Architectural plausibility assessment using documented evidence
criteria.research_action: Use the same Internet-shaped regional infrastructure, population, access workload and contemporary equipment envelope for every composition. Protocol-specific routing, discovery, caching and placement policies may differ on that infrastructure. Do not substitute a more favorable physical topology, omit regions, silently add links or assume an independently chosen cache-hit rate. Count additional equipment and its placement explicitly under the same resource envelope. An evidenced inability to serve this common setting can justify No; impossibility in every imaginable topology is not required. Missing evidence remains Pending. Documentary or bounded analytical evidence can suffice; no global simulation is required.

criteria.title: Public interoperability between independent implementations
criteria.definition: At least two independently developed implementations exchanged traffic for the selected profile in a publicly documented test. Shared standardization work does not negate implementation independence; two wrappers around the same core do not qualify. Credit only tested functions.
criteria.research_action: Identify implementers, code lineage, versions, selected profile, exchanged functions and a public test report; distinguish an interoperability goal from a completed test.

criteria.title: Published independent security analysis
criteria.definition: A third party has published a security audit or formal analysis of security-critical mechanisms of the selected profile. Identify analysis type, scope, assumptions, version and conflicts of interest. Paid independent review can qualify; publication does not imply a clean result or complete security.
criteria.research_action: Find the actual report and authorship; distinguish implementation audit, protocol analysis and formal verification. Confirm coverage of the selected composition rather than only an underlying primitive.

criteria.title: Public open-source implementation of the selected profile
criteria.definition: At least one publicly obtainable implementation covers the selected profile with its necessary implementation components available under OSI-approved licenses. Official reference status is not required. Public specifications or partial demonstration code alone do not qualify.
criteria.research_action: Locate public code, exact version, license texts, dependencies and supported profile scope. A private checkout or absent implementation files in a specification mirror does not decide public availability.

criteria.title: Published independent quantitative measurements
criteria.definition: An independent party has published at least one quantitative measurement of an implementation of the protocol, describing the scenario, method and results. The measured configuration must be identifiable and relevant to the functionality assessed. Explicitly state differences from the selected profile and the measured mechanism. Exact versions of every executable, raw data, scripts and reproduction instructions strengthen evidence but are not mandatory. Another implementation or configuration is admissible when it preserves the relevant measured mechanism. Promotional numbers without a method, exclusively theoretical results and measurements only by the evaluated implementation developers do not qualify. A Yes establishes the existence of bounded external measurements, not their favorable outcome or validation of all capabilities.
criteria.research_action: Find an independent quantitative publication with an identifiable scenario, method and results; name the measured mechanism and explain applicability and configuration differences. Exact binary pins and replay artifacts are supporting evidence, not prerequisites.

criteria.title: Real-world use by independent operators
criteria.definition: Public, attributable evidence that a person, community or organization independent of the protocol authors uses the protocol to meet a real need, beyond tests or demonstrations. Personal and community use count. There is no minimum duration or requirement to reproduce every option of the selected column. Record the actual deployment scope, version, transport and duration where known. This measures adoption, not validation of all technical properties in the column.
criteria.research_action: Find an attributable independent operator account of actual use and its purpose. Document known dates, versions and deployment components. Downloads, tutorials alone, node lists, announcements and research-only demonstrations do not suffice. Yes requires documented use; No requires confirmed absence; otherwise Pending.

criteria.title: Unprivileged routine endpoint operation
criteria.definition: A supported ordinary endpoint can perform the selected communication on an identified general-purpose OS without root/admin or equivalent elevated networking capabilities during routine operation. Disclose any privileged installation, provisioning or helper; those are not silently counted as unprivileged runtime.
criteria.research_action: Pin OS/version, endpoint role, executable, capabilities and helpers. Separate install/configure privileges from sustained operation. An untested adapter or UDP binding alone does not decide this criterion.

criteria.title: Operation without an additional kernel module
criteria.definition: A supported endpoint operates on an identified general-purpose OS without installing an additional kernel module or rebuilding its kernel. Stock networking modules and drivers are allowed; disclose required OS features and configuration.
criteria.research_action: Verify implementation installation/runtime dependencies and stock-OS support. Distinguish userspace architecture from a tested deployment and kernel configuration from an additional module.

criteria.title: Operation without specialized hardware
criteria.definition: A supported endpoint can execute the selected profile on commodity computing/network hardware, without a mandatory specialized radio, accelerator or secure element. Ordinary NICs are allowed; identify carrier constraints and do not replace the selected stack.
criteria.research_action: Document hardware requirements and a supported endpoint configuration. Optional accelerators do not negate the capability; mandatory physical-link hardware must remain in scope.

criteria.title: Create additional communication identities without network administration
criteria.definition: Over an already authorized and provisioned transport, an ordinary user can create and use additional independently controlled communication identities without network-administration privileges or modifying shared interface addresses, prefixes or routes. Identity creation must not require per-identity host-network reconfiguration or administrator provisioning. Peer acceptance and transport-access permissions remain separate. This does not promise unlimited resources, anonymity, or isolation from all resource contention.
criteria.research_action: Trace identity generation, custody and protocol use for a second ordinary user. Identify any per-identity privileged operation, shared address/interface mutation or administrator allocation. Credit only identity mechanisms in the selected stack; an extra application authentication layer is not implicit. Separate this architectural capability from D01 full endpoint runtime privileges, F03 topology-dependent addressing and S02 external identity issuance.

criteria.title: Post-quantum end-to-end key establishment
criteria.definition: The selected end-to-end key-establishment construction provides documented post-quantum confidentiality against recorded-traffic decryption, using a suitable post-quantum KEM or justified hybrid construction. Identify algorithms, combiner, negotiation and downgrade conditions. This alone does not establish post-quantum authentication against active attackers.
criteria.research_action: Inspect the actual selected key-establishment suite, not identity-signature options. Verify hybrid composition and negotiation; distinguish passive confidentiality from authentication and overall protocol security.

criteria.title: Unrestricted use and implementation of the specification
criteria.definition: The publicly available specification permits use and implementation for any purpose, including commercial use, without field-of-use restrictions or individual permission. Attribution and redistribution obligations must be disclosed. Modification does not imply compatibility, conformance or endorsement. This does not require permission to republish altered normative prose as an official standard, and does not assess patent rights (L02) or implementation-code licensing (E03). Cover the required layers of the selected profile.
criteria.research_action: Verify authoritative use/implementation permissions across the selected specification layers; distinguish notices and compatibility claims from restrictions on use. Assess patent grants separately in L02.

cells.reason: Select a headless CLIENT with KNOWN_ONLY and STRICT, a clean locally provisioned database containing only authorized User records and confirmed full public keys, trusted local serial administration, no remote administrative grants to ordinary peers, and store-forward disabled. KNOWN_ONLY rejects an unknown sender before decrypt/first-contact learning; STRICT then requires a valid signature or authenticated PKI payload for admitted records. Thus a known node number alone is insufficient: an impostor must pass the retained full-key check. For bounded revocation, persist the revoked node number in ignore_incoming while retaining its key binding, verify saved policy, then restart before declaring cutover. Ignore checks precede admission; restart discards volatile radio, deferred-dispatch and phone queues, and surviving authorized records remain usable. A new sender number still fails KNOWN_ONLY. This uses native controls and the restart allowed by F16, not an external firewall or added application authentication. It is not the default ALL policy, zero-interruption revocation, a generic arbitrary-NodeDB allowlist, or revocation of data already delivered.

cells.reason: A constructive native configuration resolves F16 without treating an application message validator as an admission gate. The dedicated receiver opens no CADET listening port and creates bidirectional channels only toward locally authorized peer public keys. channel_create passes the exact destination to the service; the channel belongs to that destination tunnel, whose key derivation includes its public identity. Validated plaintext is looked up in the channel map of that tunnel, not a global channel-number namespace. Unsolicited incoming channels at unopened ports remain unbound; the native plaintext-data handler drops data when neither local owner nor destination client exists. Thus an authorized remote peer can send payload on the locally initiated channel, while another peer cannot acquire the same local delivery path merely by choosing the same port or channel number. For revocation, stop the consuming clients and local CADET service, wait for termination, discard the old volatile delivery/channel state, and restart with no listening ports and channels only to the revised authorized set. This completed cutover removes active and queued delivery authority; authorized communication resumes on new channels. F16 permits administrative restart and does not require remote initiation or uninterrupted availability. This does not establish a general incoming-server allowlist, live channel-revocation safety or a tested GNUnet deployment. The earlier connect-callback lifetime and optional MQ-validator limitations remain valid but are not used by this witness.

cells.reason: A bounded staged-pull witness carries the same named signed Data from producer A through caches B and C to final requester D. cells.reason: The newer pinned ION API returns bundleSourceEid, primaryIntegrityVerified and payloadAuthVerified together with the ADU. Native BIB verification sets the indicators after successful processing of the corresponding target; receiver rules select keys using the bundle source EID. With exact source-specific rules and distinct sender/receiver-only keys, protected primary and payload, and the application using the source as authenticated only when both indicators are true, this supplies native final-source provenance without another authentication exchange. Unlike F16, F21 does not require all unauthenticated payloads to be stopped before the API. The previous mandatory-delivery-gate blocker conflated those criteria. Unflagged deliveries remain unauthenticated. This is shared-key peer authentication, not civil identity, nonrepudiation or replay prevention.

cells.reason: An ordinary LeaseSet advertises tunnel entry points for one Destination. Meta LeaseSets go further: they can refer to several Destinations or nested Meta LeaseSets for a common service. cells.reason: The protocol author confirms that clients calculate their trajectories using negotiated availability and transport capacity. Each client negotiates capacity, QoS and bandwidth reservation with the aggregators along its half of the path up to the rendezvous; the opposite client does the same for the other half. Known future availability and usable capacity therefore feed local trajectory selection, including whether the intended transfer fits the selected opportunities. Planning need not be performed by a central service or by one participant with the entire end-to-end contact plan. This author-confirmed architectural composition supplies the capability omitted by the earlier review, which assessed availability windows and resource observations separately.
cells.method: Direct protocol-author clarification and architectural composition assessment; no runtime test
cells.source_label: Protocol author, conversation of 2026-10-23; exact statement preserved in round581-sources.json
cells.qualification: Architectural Yes based explicitly on the author clarification, not an independently demonstrated wire or executable planner. Each side is responsible for negotiating its own half; knowledge or authority over the other half is not assumed. A local feasible plan is not by itself a global delivery guarantee: rendezvous coordination, custody where required, current agreements and compatible delivery timing still matter. This does not assign a global clock, atomic reservation protocol, numeric opcode or stale-plan recovery procedure. Concrete capacity accounting, validity and change handling remain implementation/profile obligations. F32 does not require guaranteed bandwidth or a particular SABR algorithm. The clarification establishes a composed planning capability; it does not turn a resource report or the retention mechanism alone into a reservation service.

cells.reason: Yes for an explicitly layered access topology within the selected recursive, encrypted normal-DIF composition. Let the physical route be A-X-Y-Z-B. Access DIF L contains A, X and Y; middle DIF M contains A, Y, Z and B, with its A-Y adjacency carried by the L flow through X. The selected upper DIF contains only endpoint hosts A and B. X is the first intermediary and belongs only to L. After removing its own ingress protection, X sees the L destination Y, while the serialized M PDU containing destination B remains encrypted under the A-Y adjacency keys. IRATI rmt.c protects the serialized PDU before passing it to the lower IPCP; the default crypto policy encrypts the complete current DU buffer. Receive processing removes that protection before reading the destination and dispatching management or data PDUs. Thus the boundary protects the M header, not just the application payload. The directory replicated to X is L's directory of locally registered higher-layer IPCPs, not M's directory or the upper application directory. This is a constructive architectural/source inference, not a packet-capture result.

Do not register final application names in L or query an external destination directory through X in cleartext. cells.reason: RFC 6550 sections 3.2.3 and 10.1 explicitly allow unsecured-mode RPL to rely on link-layer security. The previously unspecified access-controlled link is now bound to encrypted IEEE 802.15.4 data frames, rather than authentication alone. Linux v6.12 defines ENC_MIC128 as level 7. Its llsec_key_alloc selects ccm(aes), and llsec_do_encrypt_auth separates the MAC header as associated data from the payload passed to crypto_aead_encrypt when the ENC bit is set. The TX path invokes this function before transmission. Thus the 6LoWPAN dispatch/compression/fragment fields and the carried IPv6, ICMPv6 and RPL control fields are inside the encrypted MAC payload. This includes established DIS/DIO/DAO/DAO-ACK traffic when carried in the configured protected data frames. The positive finding uses the same visible-outer-framing allowance as C03-MQ/LP.
cells.method: Explicit configuration selection and clear/encrypted field mapping; no runtime execution
cells.source_label: RFC 6550 and Linux v6.12 link-security source, reviewed 2026-10-22
cells.qualification: This is a documentary mechanism/configuration witness, not a complete Linux RPL/DTLS executable qualification or radio capture. All relevant adjacencies and multicast transmissions must use the selected encryption policy; access control, MIC-only levels 1-3, or a mix of protected data with plaintext RPL controls does not satisfy it. Frame-control fields, MAC addresses, auxiliary security headers, frame counters/key selectors, sizes and timing remain observable. MAC acknowledgements and other link-management frames are not claimed hidden; the inspected Linux path even marks control-frame security support as incomplete. A locally captured pre-encryption TX packet is not proof of plaintext over the air. Link-key holders and forwarding routers can read RPL and IP routing information. No active-probe defense, endpoint-location anonymity, PQ protection, unprivileged operation, or traffic-analysis resistance is inferred. Keys and frame-counter lifecycle require correct provisioning. C02/F14, C04, D01 and the complete-stack execution evidence are unchanged; this is not an assertion that RPL unsecured mode encrypts itself.

cells.reason: In the explicitly selected CLIENT/ALL relay mode, a valid outer radio packet with an unknown channel hash can take DECODE_OPAQUE and OPAQUE_RELAY_ONLY. cells.reason: An explicit provisioned hierarchy resolves the previously missing all-role inventory. Partition one locally assigned ULA /48 recursively into binary subdomains. Each router maintains a local discard route for its own aggregate and redistributes only that aggregate upward; it learns only its immediate child aggregates and the root /48 from its parent. It advertises only the root /48 downward. Exact-prefix/interface filters prevent leaf specifics from propagating globally. Leaf connected LAN routes override the local discard aggregate. For a reachable destination outside the local subtree, the root /48 takes traffic upward; at the lowest containing ancestor, more-specific child routes take it downward to the leaf. Every transit role, including the root, stores only local partitions, not the complete catalog of independently originated remote subdomains or leaf LANs. Babel source/feasibility records likewise cover only accepted parent/child origins under these filters; neighbor, local redistribution and temporary withdrawal state remain bounded by local degree for the fixed topology. A withdrawn child route first has unreachable hold state, then falls into the local discard aggregate rather than back toward the parent. Native prefix/interface filters and static-route redistribution support this construction without a new overlay or control service. cells.reason: The unprivileged NET/ROM application socket does not cover the selected endpoint control plane. In the pinned ax25-tools source, netromd receives NODES announcements and calls receive_nodes; netromr.c installs learned entries using SIOCADDRT. Periodically, netromd calls transmit_nodes; netromt.c invokes SIOCNRDECOBS to age routes. Linux v6.12 nr_ioctl explicitly checks capable(CAP_NET_ADMIN) on both commands, returning EPERM otherwise. These checks occur when the recurring operations execute, not only when a socket is opened or the interface installed. The identified Linux/netromd configuration therefore does not satisfy D01: routine operation needs an elevated network-administration actor. Moving that actor into a helper would not make the complete endpoint unprivileged under the existing criterion.

cells.reason: No for the selected IRATI direct application API at the pinned revision. Dynamic application naming is present: registration supplies a name to an already assigned IPCP and does not allocate an interface address per name. However, rina_register_common opens another control descriptor through rina_open and irati_open_ctrl_port, which opens the shared control device read/write. The decisive additional trace is kernel/kipcm.c: the same dispatch table registers create-IPCP, destroy-IPCP and assign-to-DIF commands. ctrldev_write dispatches caller-selected kernel message types without an implemented permission check. The corresponding handlers invoke kipcm_ipc_create, kipcm_ipc_destroy or the IPCP assignment operation without checking the caller against a management principal. The sender control port is used for the response, not an authorization check. Therefore granting the direct device access required by registration also grants access to network-management operations. Denying that access blocks this API. This concrete authority coupling fails D04's requirement that additional identities be usable by an ordinary user without network-administration authority; it is not an inference from a failed search for documentation.
