cells.reason: The previously unspecified end-to-end group now has an explicit versioned witness. Go 1.26.5 selects X25519MLKEM768 with both modern endpoints under the default preference list. Its pinned key schedule concatenates the ML-KEM shared secret followed by the X25519 secret and passes that result into the TLS 1.3 handshake-secret derivation; the client performs the matching decapsulation and concatenation. The official libp2p TLS identity component retains certificate-chain and expected-Peer-ID verification and disables session tickets. A local QUIC execution using that component negotiated group 4588 at both ends, authenticated both peer keys and exchanged 256 useful bytes in each direction without resumption. This is sufficient for the documented passive recorded-traffic confidentiality construction in K01, within the assumptions of X25519/ML-KEM and TLS 1.3.

cells.reason: Pinned i2pd 2.58.0 implements type-6 end-to-end ratchet establishment. NewSessionReplyMessage first mixes the X25519 ephemeral agreement, encapsulates to the received ML-KEM key, authenticates the ciphertext in the transcript and calls MixKey on the KEM secret. It then mixes the additional X25519 agreement before deriving directional ratchet keys and the reply payload key. HandleNewOutgoingSessionReply performs matching decapsulation and key derivation. Crypto.cpp implements MixKey using HKDF with the current chaining key and the 32-byte secret. This supports a documentary Yes for the selected hybrid key establishment against passive recorded-traffic decryption, subject to the component cryptographic assumptions. It is an endpoint ratchet construction, not an inference from adjacent-router NTCP2 protection.

cells.reason: A licensed source-defined protocol path closes the earlier specification-rights gap without assigning the portal license to the separate specs repository. The selected go-libp2p v0.50.0 witness supplies MIT-licensed TLS identity-extension schemas, signing and verification rules, Peer ID construction, public-key protobuf schema, QUIC integration and ConnectionGater interfaces. Its pinned multiformats dependencies supply MIT-licensed multistream-select framing and negotiation, multihash encoding and multiaddr encoding definitions. The protobuf wire-format implementation is BSD-3-Clause licensed. IETF implementation permissions cover IP, UDP, QUIC and TLS; the selected quic-go dependency is also MIT licensed. These embedded definitions provide a route to use and implement the selected interfaces for any purpose, including commercial use, under the stated notices. This is the same source-defined-definition approach accepted for other stacks, rather than treating software availability alone as permission to copy unrelated specifications.

cells.reason: A licensed protocol-definition path is available in the pinned sources, rather than relying on permission to reuse website prose. BSD-3-Clause notices cover tailcfg registration/map schemas, controlclient registration and map exchanges, controlhttp/controlbase transport and handshake definitions, discovery framing, DERP frames and flow, and Tailnet Lock authority updates, signatures, synchronization and RPC schemas in tka and tailcfg/tka.go. These embedded definitions can be used and adapted commercially with the stated notices. The selected WireGuard dependency is pinned by go.mod and provides its message/handshake definitions under MIT; Noise section 16 dedicates its specification to the public domain. IP, UDP, TCP, HTTP, TLS, JSON and CBOR use IETF implementation permissions. Enrollment exposes an AuthURL/follow-up boundary: the external identity provider remains external, rather than requiring reproduction of its private business logic. OpenID Connect separately grants implementation use in Appendix C; it is not asserted to be the only provider supported. This establishes L01 at the documented protocol-interface level using the same source-embedded-definition approach accepted elsewhere in the matrix.
